description: Change of use from single family dwellinghouse to mixed use of 1 x 3 bed self-contained flat and 1x 4 person HMO; external alterations
decision_conditions: <p><span style="font-size:11pt">The principle of the proposed subdivision of the existing single family dwellinghouse into 1 x 3-bedroom self-contained flat (C3) and 1 x 4-bedroom House in Multiple Occupation HMO (C4) is unacceptable due to the site’s location in an established single family neighbourhood and poor accessibility to public transport (PTAL 2), and would represent a form of development which would result in an incompatible relationship between uses, over-intensive in its occupation and be at odds with the prevailing character of the area which is predominantly single family dwellinghouses. The proposed development is contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies GR1, HO2 and &nbsp;HO10 of Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).&nbsp;&nbsp;</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size:11pt">The proposed conversion of the first and second floor from part of a single family dwellinghouse (Class C3) to a 4-bedroom House in Multiple Occupation (HMO) (Class C4) for up to 4no. persons (as labelled on the submitted plans) would result in a substandard form of residential accommodation. The proposed HMO accommodation fails to provide any adequate internal or external amenity space for use by future occupiers, resulting in poor quality living accommodation which fails to address the daily living needs of the proposed occupants. In this way, the proposal is contrary to Policy HO10(5), (6), (7) of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size:11pt">The proposed development, by reason of absence of information relating to Flood Risk in order to demonstrate the proposal’s impact on the medium surface water flood risk zone is unacceptable and contrary to Policy CN4 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).&nbsp;</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size:11pt">The proposed development, by reason of the absence of information submitted to demonstrate safe access and egress of the proposed off-street vehicle car parking space, in conjunction with the proposed siting of the bin stores and cycle storage to the application site’s frontage, would result in adverse impact on highway safety in terms of occupiers’ and visitors’ unimpeded pedestrian access to the application site and highway safety of wider pedestrian users of the footpath along Merton Road. The proposed development is contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy D3 and Policy T4(f) of the London Plan (2021) and Policies GR1, M1 and CE1(B) of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size:11pt"><span style="line-height:normal"><span calibri="">The </span></span>cumulative impacts of the proposed off-street car parking space, bin stores and cycle storage required to adequately serve the proposed development in accordance with Council’s requirements, cannot be satisfactorily provided within the frontage of the application site and there is limited scope for soft landscaping to the site frontage. Officers are not satisfied that the waste storage, as shown on the submitted proposed site plan, would be adequate in quantum to serve the proposed development. The proposed development would result in visual clutter to the frontage of the site which will be detrimental to the character and appearance of the area. The proposal is therefore contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy D3 and D6 (Table 3.2, Part VI) of the London Plan (2021), and Policies GR1, HO2.2(f) and (j), HO10(4) and CE1 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).&nbsp;</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size:11pt">The vertical stacking of the proposed accommodation is such that the kitchen of the HMO would be positioned above one of the bedrooms of the ground floor self-contained flat resulting in transfer of noise to a principal habitable room. The application is not supported by an independent Noise Assessment to otherwise demonstrate how noise transference would be mitigated between the proposed ground floor 3-bed self-contained flat and the proposed first and second floor 4-bedroom HMO. Notwithstanding, the increased comings and goings resulting from the significant increase in occupation (to at least 10no. persons) of the application site would result in detrimental impact on the amenity of neighbouring properties in terms of noise and disturbance. This is contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policies D3, D6 and D14 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy GR1.C, Policy HO2.2(f) and Policy HO10(4) of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).&nbsp;</span></p>
